summary: Four studies directly apply boosted decision-tree ensembles (gradient boosted trees) to predicting electricity consumption, the energy-demand forecasting task; they are ranked first, most recent evidence first. [V0133] (Adebayo et al., 2026) applies boosted decision-tree ensembles to electricity consumption prediction on GridWatch, reporting 0.73 AUROC. [V0136] (Duarte et al., 2020) reports a boosted decision-tree ensembles approach for electricity consumption on ChurnBench with MAE 0.94 (note: MAE is an error metric and not directly comparable to the accuracy/F1/AUROC figures reported elsewhere). [V0135] (Chen et al., 2019) evaluates boosted decision-tree ensembles for electricity consumption on FireScope, achieving accuracy 0.87. [V0134] (Brennan et al., 2018) is a deployment study comparing baselines with boosted decision-tree ensembles for electricity consumption on ProtMap, reporting F1 = 0.80. No fifth document directly applies the requested method to the requested topic, so the final slot goes to the closest topic match: [V0124] (Adebayo et al., 2026) also targets predicting electricity consumption but uses message passing over relational graphs (ChurnBench, 0.61 AUROC), making it a same-topic/different-method comparator rather than a direct application. All other candidates are excluded from the direct set because they either apply boosted trees to unrelated topics (e.g., [V0183] wildfire extent, [V0013]/[V0015] septic deterioration, [V0061] fraud), target electricity consumption with other methods ([V0126], [V0127] self-attention encoders; [V0144] paired representation learning), or merely mention boosted decision-tree ensembles for electricity consumption as prior work without applying it ([V0099], [V0073], [V0049], [V0041], [V0034]).
